The solution builds successfully. Here's a summary of what was created:

## ShipmentTracker — Blazor Web App

**Architecture:** Auto render mode (InteractiveServer on first visit for fast load, then WebAssembly for snappy client-side interactivity — no server round-trips after initial load).

**Key files created/modified:**

| File | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `Client/Models/ShipmentDto.cs` | Shared shipment model + `ShipmentStatus` enum |
| `Data/Shipment.cs` | EF Core entity with indexed tracking# and email |
| `Data/SeedData.cs` | Seeds Dispatcher/Customer roles + 6 sample shipments |
| `Endpoints/ShipmentEndpoints.cs` | REST API — CRUD with role-based auth |
| `Client/Pages/Home.razor` | Landing page with role-aware navigation cards |
| `Client/Pages/DispatcherDashboard.razor` | Filter/search/create/update shipments (Dispatcher role) |
| `Client/Pages/TrackShipment.razor` | Customer tracking with progress visualization |

**Auth:** ASP.NET Identity with Individual accounts + `Dispatcher`/`Customer` roles. Claims are serialized to WASM via `SerializeAllClaims`. After registering a user, assign the Dispatcher role to grant dashboard access.

**To run:** `cd ShipmentTracker && dotnet run --project ShipmentTracker`
